prompt_caching.simple_definition: Storing previously processed prompt text in server memory so the AI doesn't re-read static instructions on every turn.
prompt_caching.eli5: Imagine you order the same coffee every morning. The barista already knows your order, so they don't ask again. They just make it.
prompt_caching.real_life_analogy: Ordering your regular coffee at a cafe. They remember your milk preference instead of asking you to explain it from scratch every single day.
prompt_caching.business_explanation: Reduces API token costs by 50% to 90% on repeated system prompts, saving millions of rupees on recurring enterprise workloads.
prompt_caching.technical_explanation: Calculates cryptographic hashes over prefix token sequences. Matches are loaded directly from GPU KV cache memory, bypassing the Transformer prefill attention phase.
prompt_caching.sarvax_example: SARVAX sends a 20,000-token system prompt containing compliance rules and portfolio guidelines. Prompt caching ensures SARVAX only pays full price once.
prompt_caching.when_to_use: High-volume workflows with identical system prompts, standard document templates, or long conversation histories.
prompt_caching.when_not_to_use: Dynamic, highly changing prompts shorter than 1,024 tokens where cache lookup overhead exceeds prefill time.
advantages: Cuts input token costs by up to 90%
limitations: 5-minute cache TTL expiration on standard endpoints
prompt_caching.cost_impact: Massive Cost Reduction (Reduces input token price from ₹250.50 to ₹25.05 per 1M tokens).

batch_api.simple_definition: Submitting a large queue of requests to be processed asynchronously overnight in exchange for a 50% discount.
batch_api.eli5: Like dropping off your laundry to be washed overnight instead of doing an emergency 1-hour express wash.
batch_api.real_life_analogy: Sending mail via standard economy delivery instead of express overnight courier. It takes a little longer, but costs half the price.
batch_api.business_explanation: Allows enterprises to process bulk reports, background audits, and portfolio analysis at a flat 50% discount on all token costs.
batch_api.technical_explanation: Requests are enqueued in provider worker pools during off-peak GPU utilization windows with a 24-hour non-deterministic SLA.
batch_api.sarvax_example: SARVAX generates 100,000 monthly wealth reports overnight via Batch API, slashing server bills from ₹27.14 Lakhs to ₹2.50 Lakhs.
batch_api.when_to_use: Asynchronous background jobs, cron tasks, weekly portfolio audits, and large-scale data extraction.
batch_api.when_not_to_use: Realtime user interfaces (OneChat) where the user is waiting for an instant response.
advantages: Flat 50% cost reduction across input and output tokens
batch_api.cost_impact: Direct 50% Reduction in Total Infrastructure Expense.

context_window.simple_definition: The maximum amount of text (tokens) an AI model can read and remember in a single interaction.
context_window.eli5: Like how many pages of a book you can keep in your mind at once without forgetting the beginning.
context_window.real_life_analogy: A workbench. A larger workbench lets you spread out 10 full binders side-by-side instead of stacking them.
context_window.business_explanation: Determines whether an AI can ingest a full 100-page bank statement or SEC filing without chopping it into pieces.
context_window.technical_explanation: Maximum sequence length bounded by GPU VRAM allocations for quadratic $O(N^2)$ or linear $O(N)$ attention mechanisms.
context_window.sarvax_example: Gemini 3 Pro's 2,000,000 token context window allows SARVAX to ingest 5 full years of client tax returns and portfolio reports in one prompt.
context_window.when_to_use: Analyzing multi-page contracts, legal discovery, full codebases, and historical financial transcripts.
context_window.when_not_to_use: Short single-question queries where sending huge context inflates latency and token cost unnecessarily.
limitations: Needle-in-a-haystack retrieval degradation if context is noisy
context_window.cost_impact: Linear increase in total input tokens billed per request.

graphrag.simple_definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation that builds an interconnected knowledge graph of entities and relationships rather than matching plain text chunks.
graphrag.eli5: Instead of searching for matching words in a pile of papers, it builds a detective board showing who is connected to whom.
graphrag.real_life_analogy: A company organization chart or family tree showing direct connections between people, roles, and accounts.
graphrag.business_explanation: Prevents AI hallucinations in complex wealth management by understanding how holding companies, trusts, and tax accounts link together.
graphrag.technical_explanation: Combines LLM entity extraction with graph clustering algorithms (Leiden) to generate hierarchical community summaries.
graphrag.sarvax_example: SARVAX uses GraphRAG to map a high-net-worth client's holding companies, trusts, and offshore accounts to recommend tax harvesting.
graphrag.when_to_use: Complex multi-document financial intelligence, corporate due diligence, and risk mapping.
graphrag.when_not_to_use: Simple single-document keyword search where standard vector RAG is faster and cheaper.
graphrag.cost_impact: Slightly higher indexing cost, but dramatically lowers token usage during final reasoning.

mcp.simple_definition: An open standard that connects AI models to external tools, databases, and enterprise software securely.
mcp.eli5: Like a universal USB plug that lets the AI connect to any software in your office.
mcp.real_life_analogy: A universal adapter plug that lets your phone charger fit into wall outlets in any country in the world.
mcp.business_explanation: Allows SARVAX agents to safely read and write to Salesforce, HubSpot, Morningstar, and core banking systems without custom API code.
mcp.technical_explanation: Client-server protocol utilizing JSON-RPC over stdio or HTTP SSE for dynamic tool auto-discovery, prompt templates, and resource access.
mcp.sarvax_example: SARVAX uses an MCP server to fetch live stock prices from Morningstar and automatically update the client's Salesforce CRM record.
mcp.when_to_use: Integrating AI agents with external SaaS platforms, databases, and enterprise APIs.
mcp.when_not_to_use: Isolated offline tasks that require zero external data access.
advantages: Zero custom API integration code required
limitations: Tool discovery adds minor latency overhead
mcp.cost_impact: Neutral on token costs, but slashes engineering integration hours by 80%.

agent.simple_definition: An autonomous AI software worker that can plan, make decisions, use tools, and execute multi-step business tasks.
agent.eli5: Like a digital assistant that doesn't just answer your questions, but actually goes and does the work for you.
agent.real_life_analogy: A junior financial analyst who receives a task, searches the web, checks company databases, drafts a report, and sends it to you for review.
agent.business_explanation: Shifts AI from passive chatbots ('User operates AI') to autonomous business execution ('AI operates work'), recovering thousands of person-hours.
agent.technical_explanation: Looping state machine combining LLM reasoning, long-term vector memory, tool schema execution (MCP/JSON), and self-correction reflection loops.
agent.sarvax_example: SARVAX deploys an autonomous Due Diligence Agent that crawls news, extracts financial records, checks regulatory compliance, and drafts a report.
agent.when_to_use: Multi-step workflows requiring tool integration, web research, file management, and autonomous decision making.
agent.when_not_to_use: Deterministic, single-step data operations where a fixed code script is faster, cheaper, and 100% predictable.
advantages: Adapts autonomously to unexpected document layouts
agent.cost_impact: Consumes 3x-8x more tokens than simple chat, but recovers 90%+ of human operational costs.

structured_outputs.simple_definition: Forcing the AI to format its answer in strict, machine-readable JSON data schemas.
structured_outputs.eli5: Like giving the AI a form with boxes where it MUST fill in each field cleanly without adding extra chatty text.
structured_outputs.real_life_analogy: A tax filing form. Every number must go into its exact designated box, or the tax department rejects the submission.
structured_outputs.business_explanation: Ensures AI outputs can be directly ingested into enterprise CRMs (Salesforce/HubSpot) and core banking software without breaking API integrations.
structured_outputs.technical_explanation: Constrains LLM token generation using context-free grammars (CFG) or JSON Schema token sampling logits masks at the decoder level.
structured_outputs.sarvax_example: SARVAX extracts client passport details and automatically formats them into a strict JSON payload for KYC compliance processing.
structured_outputs.when_to_use: Extracting form data, CRM writeback, database population, and feeding downstream code scripts.
structured_outputs.when_not_to_use: Creative, open-ended research writing where freeform Markdown prose is preferred.
advantages: Zero JSON parse errors in backend code
structured_outputs.cost_impact: Neutral on pricing, but eliminates API integration error recovery costs.

tau_banking.simple_definition: An independent, rigorous benchmark that tests how accurately an AI model performs complex banking and financial advisory tasks.
tau_banking.eli5: A tough exam specifically designed for bank managers and wealth advisors.
tau_banking.real_life_analogy: The Certified Financial Planner (CFP) exam testing a wealth manager's knowledge of tax law, portfolio allocation, and banking rules.
tau_banking.business_explanation: Identifies which AI models can be trusted with actual customer money, tax calculations, and wealth management advice.
tau_banking.technical_explanation: Multi-step tool-use and mathematical evaluation suite measuring accuracy across banking API interactions, ledger balances, and compliance constraints.
tau_banking.sarvax_example: Kimi K3 ranks #1 globally on TAU Banking (0.3340), leading SARVAX to select it as the primary financial reasoning engine.
tau_banking.when_to_use: Evaluating models for wealth management, banking chatbots, tax planning, and credit underwriting.
tau_banking.when_not_to_use: General creative writing or coding tasks where SWE-bench or MMLU-Pro are better indicators.
advantages: Directly measures financial services domain competence
Tests math and tool execution together
limitations: Evolving test set requiring continuous validation
tau_banking.cost_impact: Guides model selection to maximize accuracy per rupee spent.

react_loop.simple_definition: An iterative execution cycle where an AI agent alternates between thinking, executing tool calls, observing outputs, and adjusting its next action.
react_loop.eli5: Imagine a detective solving a puzzle: they think of a clue, look for evidence, read what they found, and then decide what to check next until the mystery is solved.
react_loop.real_life_analogy: A financial advisor reviewing a tax statement: they check income, calculate deductions, look up new tax brackets, and then draft the final tax return.
react_loop.business_explanation: Powers multi-step autonomous AI workers capable of executing complex enterprise workflows without human step-by-step guidance.
react_loop.technical_explanation: Combines step-by-step chain-of-thought prompting with dynamic JSON tool call execution, maintaining an active state history across $N$ execution turns.
react_loop.sarvax_example: SARVAX agents use ReAct loops to fetch client accounts from Salesforce, query Morningstar for stock valuations, and calculate portfolio rebalancing options.
react_loop.when_to_use: Complex multi-step workflows requiring tool interactions, web searches, and dynamic decision trees.
react_loop.when_not_to_use: Simple single-prompt tasks where a direct answer is needed without tool interactions.
advantages: Adapts dynamically to unexpected API tool errors
limitations: Potential for infinite retry loops if un-guarded
react_loop.cost_impact: Multiplies token usage per task by 3x-6x, but slashes human execution hours by 90%.
official_sources: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models (arXiv:2210.03629)

speculative_decoding.simple_definition: Using a tiny, fast drafting model to generate candidate tokens, which a larger model then verifies in a single parallel batch.
speculative_decoding.eli5: A fast assistant writes a quick rough draft, and the senior boss quickly checks and approves 5 words at a time instead of typing letter by letter.
speculative_decoding.real_life_analogy: An intern drafting a routine email signature and opening statement, which the senior partner reviews in 2 seconds.
speculative_decoding.business_explanation: Speeds up large model response time by 2x to 3x without degrading quality or increasing hardware cost.
speculative_decoding.technical_explanation: Speculatively samples $K$ tokens from a lightweight draft model $M_{\text{draft}}$, running a single parallel verification pass on target model $M_{\text{target}}$.
speculative_decoding.sarvax_example: SARVAX uses Gemini Flash as a drafting model for Kimi K3, reducing wealth advisory report generation latency from 12s to 4s.
speculative_decoding.when_to_use: High-latency reasoning models in interactive user chat sessions.
speculative_decoding.when_not_to_use: Batch background jobs where latency is unimportant.
speculative_decoding.cost_impact: Neutral on token price, dramatically reduces TTFT latency.
official_sources: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding (arXiv:2211.17192)
